findings.text: So he was honest and worn out, but she still couldn't have told him from a man who was worn out and paid, not from the arch.
findings.pattern: NEG-P4 buried trailing negation (camouflage: after a comma)
findings.deletionTest: So he was honest and worn out, but she still couldn't have told him from a man who was worn out and paid.
findings.reason: The tacked-on 'not from the arch' is a negation qualifier in a paragraph already carrying 'nobody needed it' and 'Nobody could order'. The vantage limit can be stated positively.
findings.suggestedFix: So he was honest and worn out, though from the arch she couldn't have told him from a man who was worn out and paid.

findings.text: He wasn't tall, but broad and square, with the build of a man who had carried sacks before he ever carried a truncheon.
findings.pattern: NEG-P1 direct contrast pivot (not X but Y)
findings.deletionTest: He was broad and square, with the build of a man who had carried sacks before he ever carried a truncheon.
findings.reason: Textbook 'not X but Y'. The sentence works from 'broad and square'.
findings.suggestedFix: He was of middle height, broad and square, with the build of a man who had carried sacks before he ever carried a truncheon.

findings.text: She didn't hurry. The loader was well ahead of her and in no hurry himself, the leather pad on his shoulder showing pale in the dusk, walking up the middle of the lane.
findings.pattern: NEG-P5 preamble negation, mirrored ('didn't hurry' / 'in no hurry himself')
findings.deletionTest: The loader was well ahead of her, the leather pad on his shoulder showing pale in the dusk, walking up the middle of the lane.
findings.reason: Both her pace and his are given by what they were not doing, back to back. State the pace.
findings.suggestedFix: She matched the loader's pace. He was well ahead of her, walking easy up the middle of the lane, the leather pad on his shoulder showing pale in the dusk.

findings.text: The fingers Tam had bitten wouldn't close properly on it; they caught the edge late and held badly.
findings.pattern: NEG-P5 preamble negation (negative then the positive restatement)
findings.deletionTest: The fingers Tam had bitten caught the edge late and held badly.
findings.reason: The second clause already carries the damaged grip. The negative half is scaffolding.
findings.suggestedFix: The fingers Tam had bitten caught the edge late and held badly.

findings.text: On the side of the nearest she could make out a sheaf in a ring, stencilled, and letters under it that she didn't need to read.
findings.pattern: NEG-P4 minimizer (recognition stated as a need she did not have)
findings.deletionTest: On the side of the nearest she could make out a sheaf in a ring, stencilled, and letters under it.
findings.reason: The coy negation stands in for 'she recognised it'. The next sentence (her hand on the Brask sacking) carries the recognition.
findings.suggestedFix: On the side of the nearest she could make out a sheaf in a ring, stencilled, with lettering under it that she knew.

findings.text: At the top of the sheet, above where his hand began, were three lines that weren't his: blots, a stroke that had gone through the paper, a word she couldn't make out at all.
findings.pattern: NEG-P4 redundant negation (already implied by 'above where his hand began')
findings.deletionTest: At the top of the sheet, above where his hand began, were three lines: blots, a stroke that had gone through the paper, a word she couldn't make out at all.
findings.reason: Deletion test passes; 'above where his hand began' and Jaina's 'I tried' already say whose lines they are.
findings.suggestedFix: At the top of the sheet, above where his hand began, were three lines: blots, a stroke that had gone through the paper, a word she couldn't make out at all.

findings.text: The three from the gate didn't go in. They went up Hurdle Lane.
findings.deletionTest: The three from the gate went up Hurdle Lane.
findings.reason: Deletion test passes. The contrast with the pair who 'went in last' survives without the negative sentence.
findings.suggestedFix: The three from the gate went up Hurdle Lane instead.

findings.text: The mouth of Tenter Row came on the right, narrower than the rest.
findings.pattern: IS-P1 geography given a motion verb (second sweep)
findings.subject: the mouth of Tenter Row
findings.realAgent: Sylvanas and Havel walking down Hurdle Lane reached it
findings.reason: The lane mouth does the moving while the walkers drop out. A plain locative fixes it.
findings.suggestedFix: On the right was the mouth of Tenter Row, narrower than the rest.

findings.text: She put her weight on the other two and her forearm and went up anyway, lying flat on the slates at the top with grit in her cheek and her heart going harder than the climb deserved.
findings.pattern: IS-P5 abstraction given judgment ('the climb deserved')
findings.subject: the climb
findings.realAgent: Sylvanas's own body after a short climb; nothing judges anything
findings.reason: The climb is given a judgment verb. State the mismatch plainly.
findings.suggestedFix: She put her weight on the other two and her forearm and went up anyway, lying flat on the slates at the top with grit in her cheek and her heart going hard for so short a climb.

findings.text: He bent and put his gloved hand into it, and it came out full of something dark and thick that hung off his fingers like cold dripping.
findings.pattern: IS-P8 body part as subject ('it [the hand] came out')
findings.subject: his gloved hand
findings.realAgent: the masked man drew his hand out
findings.reason: Put the character back in subject position and the sentence means the same. This is the deliberate act at the centre of the scene, so it should be his act.
findings.suggestedFix: He bent and put his gloved hand into it and drew it out full of something dark and thick that hung off his fingers like cold dripping.
